bindings.label: A 43-year-old man presented with multiple skin lesions on his shoulders, back, feet, and hands

The patient was a 43-year-old man who visited an outpatient endocrine clinic at Tabriz University of Medical Sciences, Tabriz, Iran, accompanied by his sister, for assessment of skin lesions; he reported no other complaints and maintained an active lifestyle as a greengrocer

The patient had multiple lesions on his shoulders, back, the lateral and medial parts of the dorsal surface of his feet, the medial and lateral malleus of both feet, and the dorsal and palmar surfaces of both hands

His siblings were monitored in the same clinic for similar skin conditions characterized by palmar, eruptive, tuberous, and trauma site xanthomas, along with elevated plasma total cholesterol and triglycerides; both parents had normal serum lipid levels; there was no history of coronary artery or other atherosclerotic disorders in the patient or his siblings
A pathology report from a skin lesion biopsy performed by a dermatologist a few months prior indicated the presence of lipid-laden macrophages
Fasting lipid panel shows total cholesterol 507 mg/dl, triglycerides 470 mg/dl, and HDL 41 mg/dl
LDL-C, Lp(a), apoB, lipoprotein electrophoresis, genetic testing, and secondary hyperlipidemia workup remain unretrieved
Secondary hyperlipidemia (e.g., hypothyroidism, diabetes mellitus, nephrotic syndrome, or drug-induced)
